sentences.text: Succinctly, the facts of the case are that on 22.04.1998 at about 11:45 p.m., Joginder Ram (since deceased) was proceeding from Shahbad to village Sulakhani on his scooter scooter bearing registration No. No.CHE-8993.

When he reached near 1 of 5 FAO-2156-2000 2000 (O&M) -2- the Markanda Old Bridge on G.T. Road, a Maruti Van bearing registration No. DAV-3077 3077 (hereinafter referred to as offending vehicle), driven by respondent No.5- Jaspal Singh, came from behind and struck the scooter of the deceased.
The said vehicle was being driven in a rash and negligent manner.
As a consequence of the impact, Joginder Ram sustained multiple injuries and succumbed to the same at the spot.
Consequently, the respondent Nos-1 Nos 1 to 4 -claimants claimants being the wife and children of the deceased, filed ed a petition claiming compensation for the same.

On 20.01.2000, vide the impugned award passed by the learned Tribunal, compensation to the tune of 4,29,500/- was awarded in their favour, holding the appellant-Insurance Insurance Company along with respondent Nos.5 and 6 (driver and owner of the Maruti Van No. DAV-3077,
DAV 3077, respectively) jointly and severally liable to pay the said amount.
amount Affected ffected by the same, appellant-Insurance Insurance Company has filed the present appeal.

3. Learned counsel for the appellant- appella -Insurance Insurance Company contended that the impugned Award, passed by the learned Tribunal, suffers from patent illegality and material infirmities and is liable to be set aside.

It was submitted by the learned counsel that respondents No.1 and 2, while admitt admitting ing the factum of accident, specifically pleaded that the accident occurred due to the rash and reckless driving of the deceased himself, which aspect has been completely ignored by the learned Tribunal.

Furthermore, Furthermore, the finding of negligence recorded agai against nst the driver of offending vehicle is based on misreading and mis mis-appreciation appreciation of evidence, as the FIR was initially registered against an unknown person.
The involvement of the offending vehicle was introduced subsequently, on the statement of PW PW-2-Bal Baldev Singh.

Moreover, Moreover,
the learned Tribunal erred in assessing the monthly income of the deceased at 3,500/-
3,500/ in the absence of any documentary evidence and further erred 2 of 5 FAO-2156-2000 2000 (O&M) -3- in applying the multiplier of 15.
Additionally Additionally,, the amounts awarded under the heads of consortium, onsortium, loss of estate and funeral expenses are excessive and unjustified.

Lastly, Lastly, the findings recorded by the learned Tribunal on all the issues are based on surmises and conjectures, are not sustainable in the eye of law and, therefore, the impugned Award deserves to be set aside.

4. Learned counsels for the respondent No.6 submitted that the accident in question did not occur due to any rash or negligent driving on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle and that the findings recorded by th thee learned Tribunal on the issues are erroneous.

It is further submitted National Ins. Co. Ltd vs Bachni Devi on 5 February, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/164371487/
2 that respondent No.6-owner owner has been wrongly held liable without proper appreciation of the evidence on record.

5. There is no representation on behalf of respondent respondents No. 1 to 4.
6.

Having heard the learned counsel for the parties and after perusing the paper book with their able assistance, this Court is of the considered view that the contentions raised on behalf of the appellant do not merit acceptance and finds no infirmity in the findings recorded by the learned Tribunal.

It is a settled proposition of law that registration of FIR is not a sine qua non for maintaining a claim petition under the Motor Vehicles Act, Act, and the claimants are only required to establish negligence on the basis of preponderance of probabilities.

In the present case, though the appellant has raised an objection regarding alleged infirmities in the FIR, the same does not affect the case of the claimants, as negligence has been duly proved by the testimony of PW-2 2 Baldev Singh, who was present at the spot and witnessed the occurrence.

He has categorically deposed that the deceased was proceeding on scooter bearing registration No. 8993 when Maruti Van bearing registration No. 3077 came from behind in a rash and negligent manner and hit the scooter,
resulting in the fall and death of the deceased at the spot.
PW PW-2 2 further 3 of 5 FAO-2156-2000 2000 (O&M) -4- stated that the driver of offending offen ing vehicle fled away after the accident.
His testimony remained intact in cross-examination cross examination and no material co contradiction ntradiction could be elicited so as to discredit his presence or version.

Though the FIR was initially recorded against an unknown vehicle but during the investigation, statement of PW-2 2 Baldev Singh was recorded by the police, who unimpeachably mentioned the make and number of the offending vehicle, on the basis of which criminal proceedings were initiated against the driver of the offending vehicle

In this regard, reliance may be placed upon the judgement of the Hon'ble Supreme Court in Ravi yan (2011) 4 SCC 693,, wherein it has been held that lodging of an v. Badrinarayan FIR is not an absolute requirement in motor accident claim cases and that delay in lodging the same cannot be a ground to deny compensation when the evidence on record inspires confidence.

The he testimony of an independent eye eye-witness, witness, who has proved the occurrence and involvement of the offending vehicle, is to be given due precedence over bald denials by the driver or owner or Insu Insurance rance Company.

In this regard, reliance may be placed upon the the judgement of this Court in United India Insurance Company Limited v. Narender Singh and others others, FAO No.3007 of 2021, decided on 07.02.2022 (2022:PHHC:009951).

Significantly, the appellant-insurance insurance company did not lead any cogent evidence to rebut the ocular version or to substantiate tthe plea that the accident occurred due to the negligence of the deceased himself and thus thus, the learned Tribunal ribunal has rightly fastened the liability upon respondent No.1 to 3 before it, jointly and severally.
With regard to to the quantum of compensation, the learned Tribunal has considered the pleadings and evidence relating to the age and income of the deceased.
Though respondent Nos.1 to 4--claimants claimants asserted a higher income, the learned Tribunal assessed the monthly income of the deceased at 3,500/-..

The 4 of 5 FAO-2156-2000 2000 (O&M) -5- deduction towards personal expenses and application of multiplier of 15 as well as compensation awarded under the conventional heads of consortium, loss of estate and funeral expenses is minimal and strictly in accordance w with ith the norms prevalent at the time of passing of the impugned Award.

It is also well settled that the learned Tribunal,
being the Court of first instance, had the advantage of observing the demeanour of the witnesses and appreciating the oral and documentary evidence in the first instance, and unless its conclusions are shown to be perverse or based on no evidence, the same deserve due weight in appellate scrutiny.
9. In view of the aforesaid facts and circumstances, this Court finds no ground to interfere with the award dated 20.01.2000 20.01.2000 passed by the learned Tribunal and the same is upheld.
Resultantly, Resultantly, the present appeal is dismissed.
10. Misc. application pending, if any, also stands disposed of.
